slides.texte_overlay:
What cold showers actually
do for your mind
They train you to stay calm under stress. The first seconds feel like panic. Learning to breathe slowly through it builds a calm you can use elsewhere.
They wake you up fast. A short cold rinse at the end of a shower clears morning fog better than scrolling in bed.
They build a daily win. Doing something uncomfortable first thing tells your brain you can handle hard things today.
They teach you about your breathing. Fast, shallow breaths make it worse. Slow exhales make it easier. That lesson works everywhere.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Pair it with your cold shower and start every morning with two wins.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Pair it with your cold shower and start every morning with two wins.

slides.texte_overlay: Start small. Thirty seconds of cold at the end of a warm shower is enough. Add a few seconds each week. Consistency matters more than intensity.
Listen to your body. Cold showers aren't for everyone. If you have a heart condition or feel unwell, ask a doctor first.
